notes: EBIT is treated as GAAP operating income (loss) from the consolidated segment reconciliation. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))
D&A is defined as depreciation + amortization of intangibles (per Intel cash flow reconciliation). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))
Capex is defined as absolute “Additions to property, plant and equipment” from the cash flow statement. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))

NWC construction (for DCF modeling) is: (Total current assets − cash & cash equivalents − short-term investments) − (Total current liabilities − short-term debt). This is a simplification and may differ from more detailed working-capital schedules. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))

tax_rate (0.12) is set to Intel’s non-GAAP tax rate disclosed alongside Q1 2026 and FY2025 results; GAAP tax rate can be distorted when earnings are negative. ([intc.com](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1759/intel-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial))
WACC (0.085) is a model assumption (not directly reported by Intel). Treat as a baseline scenario input subject to refinement if your pipeline has a standardized WACC module.

Comps multiples come from ValueSense peer-set tables; exact NTM definitions may differ from strict “next 12 months” sell-side conventions. ([valuesense.io](https://valuesense.io/ticker/amd/ev-to-revenue-ntm))

NOL carryforwards are taken from Intel’s disclosed federal and non-U.S. net operating loss carryforwards; the non-U.S. figure is presented in rounded “billion” terms in the filing. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))

catalysts: Sustained ramp in Intel 18A/advanced-node execution and foundry supply improvement beyond Q1 2026. ([intc.com](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1759/intel-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial))

Further evidence of gross margin expansion and operating expense discipline translating into positive GAAP operating income. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))

Progress on foundry customer traction and partner ecosystem that supports revenue visibility and utilization. ([intc.com](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1759/intel-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial))
company_overview: Intel operates across Intel Products (CCG and DCAI) and Intel Foundry services. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))
FY2025 net revenue was $52.853B with GAAP operating loss of $(2.214)B. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))
As of Dec 27, 2025, Intel reported $37.416B cash and short-term investments and $46.585B total debt. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))
current_context: Q4 2025 revenue was $13.7B (down 4% YoY); GAAP operating margin (loss) was 4.2% for the quarter. ([intc.com](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1759/intel-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial))

FY2025 revenue was $52.9B (flat YoY) and GAAP operating margin (loss) was (4.2)%. ([intc.com](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1759/intel-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial))

Intel guided Q1 2026 revenue to $11.7B–$12.7B (midpoint used for modeling where applicable). ([intc.com](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1759/intel-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial))

Management highlighted supply constraints expected to be lowest in Q1 before improving in Q2 and beyond. ([intc.com](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1759/intel-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes revenue stabilizes and returns to modest mid-single-digit growth after demand/supply normalization (consistent with Q1 2026 setup and improving supply expectations). ([intc.com](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1759/intel-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial))

Base case EBIT margin recovers from the 2024/2025 impairment/accelerated-depreciation impact toward a sustainable positive margin as those charges roll through. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))

Depreciation/amortization and capex remain structurally high, reflecting ongoing manufacturing investment; capex gradually normalizes as the fab build cycle matures. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))

Working capital modeled as still negative but improving (consistent with historical movement from more negative NWC in 2023/2024 toward 2025). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))
key_risks: Demand/supply mismatch and utilization risk: if product cycles or customer ramps slip, margin recovery may stall. ([intc.com](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1759/intel-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial))

Asset impairment/accelerated depreciation or restructuring charges could re-expand losses and delay EBIT normalization. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/50863/000005086326000011/intc-20251227.htm))

Macro/competitive pressures (pricing and mix) could keep EBIT margin below base case assumptions. ([intc.com](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1759/intel-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-financial))
